questions.q: Why can a flash loan be issued with zero collateral while the lender still bears no default risk?
options: Because the entire borrow-use-repay sequence happens inside one atomic transaction — if repayment fails, the whole transaction (including the original loan) reverts as if it never happened
Because flash loans are insured by a government program
Because flash loan borrowers must pass a credit check
Because the lending protocol personally guarantees repayment from its own treasury
questions.explain: Atomicity makes default mechanically impossible — a failed repayment just means the transaction never completed, not that funds were lost.

questions.q: In the callback pattern, what does the lending pool check immediately after calling executeOperation on the borrower's contract?
options: The borrower's credit score
Whether its own balance has returned to at least the amount borrowed plus the fee
Whether the borrower's contract has been audited
The current gas price on the network
questions.explain: The pool's code checks its balance right after the callback returns; if it isn't back to amount + fee, the entire transaction reverts.

questions.q: How does a flash loan let a borrower facing liquidation (from Lesson 12) avoid paying a third party's liquidation bonus?
options: It doesn't — flash loans have no connection to liquidations
By permanently canceling the loan with no repayment required
By flash-borrowing to repay their own debt and withdraw collateral themselves, before any outside liquidator can act
By transferring the debt to a different borrower
questions.explain: Self-liquidation uses a flash loan to repay the position's own debt directly, letting the original borrower keep the liquidation bonus that would otherwise go to a third-party liquidator.

questions.q: What do flash loans actually add to an attacker exploiting an existing vulnerability (like an oracle manipulation bug)?
options: A brand-new type of bug that didn't exist before
They make the attack illegal, which deters most attackers
They slow down the attack enough for defenders to react
They remove the capital constraint — the attacker no longer needs millions of their own dollars to exploit it profitably
questions.explain: The lesson is explicit: a flash loan doesn't create the vulnerability, it removes the practical capital barrier that previously limited who could exploit it.

questions.q: Which of the following is listed as a legitimate use of flash loans?
options: Collateral swap — moving a lending position from one collateral asset to another within a single transaction
Permanently borrowing funds with no repayment obligation
Avoiding gas fees entirely on a transaction
Bypassing a protocol's liquidation threshold forever
questions.explain: Collateral swap, alongside arbitrage and self-liquidation, is explicitly listed as a legitimate use case for the atomic, uncollateralized nature of flash loans.
